subject: Arboretum: evidence for 120d log request and compensating controls
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@arboretumhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@arboretumhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Initial: log retention scope and SIG evidence request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG assessment for platform onboarding we need confirmation of your customer-facing log retention behavior and artifacts showing controls. Specifically Arboretum requires 120 days of tenant-level session and request logs for compliance with our internal incident response framework.

Can you provide: 
- A short description of how Redwood retains request/session logs (where they live, retention windows, deletion triggers).
- Any SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ artifacts that map to logging/forensics controls (evidence or pointers is fine).
- If 120d cannot be supported by default, what compensating controls you can apply (snapshot exports, escrow, extended retention on request, or signed attestation).

We'd like to review this week and include the artifacts in our procurement packet.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Patel
Security & Risk, Arboretum Health
security@arboretumhealth.com

--

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial: log retention scope and SIG evidence request

Hi Maya —

Thanks for the note and the clear asks. Short answer: our standard tenant activity/request logs are retained 90 days across hosted deployments, but we have customer-specific pathways to accommodate longer windows through one of the following:

1) Temporary retention extension (managed): we can enable a 120d retention for your tenant for an agreed period via our Dedicated retention controls (requires an SLA amendment).
2) Snapshot export: we can produce periodic encrypted snapshots of tenant logs (S3-compatible export) that you can ingest into your storage for the 120d window.
3) Escrow & attestation: for customers who need evidence of deletion we provide signed proof-of-delete packages and CAIQ/SIG mappings.

I'll pull the specific SIG/SOC artifacts and propose a short compensating-controls package. Looping in Ben (Customer Security Engagement) and Karthik (Legal / Procurement support) to coordinate artifacts and the SLA amendment.

Irene Choi
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Attaching the SIG matrix slice for logging (sig_matrix_arboretum.xlsx) and a zipped evidence bundle of artifacts we can share today (evidence_bundle_arboretum_v1.zip). Contents include: logging architecture diagram, retention policy excerpt, sample anonymized request-log export (JSON stub), and our SOC 2 control mapping for CC6/CC7.

Regarding the retention path: for hosted customers we normally recommend the snapshot-export option (option #2 Irene mentioned) because making hosted tenants live-longer has operational and cost implications. Snapshot export can be automated daily, encrypted to a customer-controlled bucket, and retained by Arboretum for 120 days — we can provide a signed intake/transfer log for auditability.

If procurement insists on Redwood holding 120d natively, we'd need an SLA amendment and a cost uplift (I had ops ballpark ~1.25x for storage and retention snapshot overhead). Karthik, can you confirm contract language and pricing?

Hi Maya —

Appended is our package for Arboretum's SIG review (see attachments referenced). TL;DR: we recommend snapshot exports to your S3 bucket as the lower-friction approach. If you require Redwood to retain 120d natively we can do so with the attached SLA amendment; pricing and term are summarized in the doc. 

Summary of materials provided:
- sig_matrix_arboretum.xlsx (mapping of CAIQ/SIG questions to our artifacts and control owners)
- evidence_bundle_arboretum_v1.zip (relevant SOC 2 excerpts, diagrams, anonymized log sample, and signed attestation template)
- proposed-sla-amendment-120d.docx (draft amendment, redlineable)

Proposed compensating controls if you choose snapshot exports:
- Daily encrypted export to your customer-controlled bucket (AES-256), with transfer logs retained by Redwood for 7 days and a signed receipt delivered daily.
- Automated integrity check (SHA256) and retention-report delivered weekly.
- On-demand forensics support: Redwood will hold a pull-request runbook and a named contact for escalations (Ben Carter).

Next steps: please confirm whether you want us to enable automated exports (we can start within 48 hours after a short intake call) or whether Procurement prefers to move forward with the SLA amendment redline. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through this week.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
